about: workflow:list-what-my-ais-sent-out: keeps, in the person's own store, every thing their AIs sent out in the world (an email, post, comment, direct message, reply or order) that one of the AIs or a tool recorded, and lists them newest first, a page at a time. It replaces tools/list-everything-my-ais-sent-out-in-the-world (src/sent-tools.mjs: the list_sent and record_sent tools, whose whole job was reading and keeping the /sent records of the retired record store). The kinds that say how each record reads and where it opens are DATA in tools/keep-and-wake-ai-sessions-on-this-computer/records/sent-kinds.json and are not moved (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do).

payload.label: List what my AIs sent out
payload.job: Keep each thing an AI sent out for the person by a road that did not keep it itself, with the exact words, to whom, when, by which tool and provider, and the open link when there is one, once per id; and list what was sent, newest first, a page at a time, with the next page's cursor.
payload.produces: The store's own sent object, proven on the example sends in the store, each record kept, repeated or refused and read back, and each list page answered in order.

source.from: tools/list-everything-my-ais-sent-out-in-the-world (src/sent-tools.mjs, list_sent and record_sent), read on the workshop repository's origin/main; the old source is the /sent route of the old store
source.note: The tools checked and shaped nothing; the store route decided. The recipe keeps the same fields the tool's record_sent schema names. The kind rows (label, view, open link) stay in tools/keep-and-wake-ai-sessions-on-this-computer/records/sent-kinds.json and are read as DATA when a list is shown.

where.description: Where the person keeps these things: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

place.description: Where in the store the sent records are kept, when they already are

before.description: For list: the next_page of the page before, { value, id }

kind.description: One of the kinds in records/sent-kinds.json

to.description: Who or where it went: a text or a list of texts

body_markdown.description: The exact words that were sent

provider_account.description: Observed in source evidence; never guessed from the recorder

id.description: Its id in the sent list; a new one when left out

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit where the sent records are kept (kept_in, or null) and the names of the objects that already keep them, and show them.

steps.title: Make the store's own object, once
steps.do: When the look step found nothing, make one object in the store's own form: sent (id, kind, to, subject, body_markdown, body_html, body_text, sent_at, from, reply_to, preheader, provider, provider_id, provider_account, execution_ref, origin, open_url, task_id, tool_id, recorder, recorded_at), primary key id. The kind must be one of the kinds in records/sent-kinds.json; origin is real, synthetic or unknown; to is kept as a list of texts. Grant only what the store's holder allows the person's login. Submit the name of the object made, or the one the look step found.

steps.title: Prove the object on the example sends
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with the same object, do these in order: record {id: "sent:e1", kind: "email", to: ["sam@example.com"], subject: "Your order", body_markdown: "Thanks, it ships Monday.", sent_at: "2026-11-10T10:00:00Z", origin: "real", tool_id: "the sending tool's id"}; record {id: "sent:p1", kind: "post", to: ["the public feed"], body_markdown: "New: the note index.", sent_at: "2026-11-11T10:00:00Z", origin: "real"}; record sent:e1 again with the same body (repeated); record sent:e1 with a changed body (refused: a sent record is never rewritten); record {id: "sent:x1", kind: "telegram"} (refused: not one of the kinds); list with limit 1; list with limit 1 and the before of the first page; list with no limit. Rules: a record with an id that is kept is repeated when its words are the same and refused when they differ; to is kept as a list; the list is newest first by sent_at, then id; a page's next_page is { value: its last sent_at, id: its last id }. Then remove the throwaway place. Submit outcomes (kept, repeated or refused, in order) and answers: the first page (limit 1) is sent:p1 with next_page {value: 2026-11-11T10:00:00Z, id: sent:p1}; the page after it, read with that before, is sent:e1 with no next page; the full list is sent:p1 then sent:e1.

steps.title: Keep each run through that object
steps.do: For record: check the kind against records/sent-kinds.json, keep the record with its id (a new id when none is given), and repeat it when a kept record has the same words, refuse it when the words differ. For list: read the page newest first from the cursor, limit at most 200, and submit each record with its kind's label, view and open link from records/sent-kinds.json (a record's own open_url always wins over the template). Submit the outcome and the rows read back.

payload.erase: On the person's request the store deletes the sent records named, or all of them. Each record is the person's own record of what was sent.
